concepts.deeper: After the model produces a probability distribution over all possible next tokens, top-k keeps only the k most likely ones, and top-p (nucleus sampling) keeps the smallest set whose cumulative probability exceeds p. Both prevent the model from picking wildly improbable tokens. They're used with temperature: temperature reshapes the distribution, then top-p/top-k trim it.

rag.pm: Ground the bot in your own docs so answers cite real sources — fewer escalations, no invented policies.
rag.eng: Retrieve top-k relevant chunks via vector search and inject them into the prompt at inference time.

evals.pm: A regression suite for quality — proof a change actually moved the metric before you ship.
evals.eng: Automated graders (exact-match, rubric, or LLM-as-judge) scoring output over a fixed dataset.

contextwindow.pm: The model's attention budget — overload it and details drop, so scope what you feed it.
contextwindow.eng: Max token span the model attends over; content beyond it is truncated or must be chunked/retrieved.

hitl.pm: A human approval gate on risky actions — your control point for compliance and trust.
hitl.eng: An approval checkpoint that blocks an action until a human confirms (all / sampled / low-confidence).

agents.pm: AI that completes multi-step tasks end to end — automation you delegate outcomes to, not just answers.
agents.eng: A model-driven loop: choose action → run tool → observe result → repeat until a stop condition.

embeddings.pm: The tech behind 'find similar' — powers semantic search, dedup, and recommendations.
embeddings.eng: Dense vector representations where cosine distance approximates semantic similarity.

finetuning.pm: Teaching the model your style with examples — powerful but a maintenance cost; try prompting/RAG first.
finetuning.eng: Gradient updates on a base model (often LoRA/PEFT) over labeled examples to shift behavior.

vibecoding.pm: The 2024 name for prompt-until-it-works prototyping — now matured into agentic coding with guardrails.
vibecoding.eng: Prompt-driven codegen without close review; superseded by agent workflows with tests and specs.

promptengineering.pm: Wording requests well for better output — a fading standalone skill as models read intent better.
promptengineering.eng: Structuring prompts (instructions, examples, format constraints) to steer the output distribution.

tokens.pm: The billing and length unit for AI — costs and limits are counted in these, not words.
tokens.eng: Sub-word units from the tokenizer; model I/O and pricing are both measured per token.

hallucination.pm: Confident wrong answers — the core reliability risk; mitigate with grounding, citations, and evals.
hallucination.eng: Plausible-but-false generations from likelihood-based decoding untethered from ground truth.

mcp.pm: A standard that lets any AI plug into your tools without custom builds — faster integrations, less lock-in.
mcp.eng: An open protocol for tool/data discovery and invocation between a model host and external servers.

chainofthought.pm: Letting the model reason step by step — better accuracy on hard tasks, now built into reasoning models.
chainofthought.eng: Intermediate reasoning tokens before the answer; boosts multi-step tasks, often internalized in reasoning models.

temperature.pm: A creativity dial — low for reliable extraction, high for brainstorming variety.
temperature.eng: Softmax scaling on next-token logits; higher flattens the distribution, lower sharpens it.

promptinjection.pm: A security risk where malicious text hijacks your AI — a key reason to gate agent actions.
promptinjection.eng: Adversarial instructions in untrusted input the model executes; mitigate via isolation + approval, not solved.

contextengineering.pm: The discipline of feeding the model the right information at each step — usually the real lever behind a "smarter" agent.
contextengineering.eng: Runtime assembly of LLM input (instructions, retrieved chunks, history, tool outputs) under token and ordering constraints.

orchestration.pm: The engine that turns a model into a multi-step agent — where reliability and control actually live.
orchestration.eng: The loop/state machine coordinating model calls, tool invocation, memory, and stop conditions.

tooluse.pm: What lets an agent take real actions — the difference between an assistant that answers and one that does.
tooluse.eng: Model emits schema-conformant call requests; the runtime executes and returns results into context.

a2a.pm: An emerging standard for agents built by different teams to interoperate — less custom glue, more reuse.
a2a.eng: Open protocol: Agent Cards for discovery, task-oriented async messaging with streaming updates.

llmjudge.pm: A way to measure fuzzy quality at scale — proof a change helped, without hand-grading everything.
llmjudge.eng: A grader model scores outputs against a rubric over a fixed eval set; validate against human labels.

grounding.pm: Anchoring answers in your real sources — the biggest lever for trust and fewer wrong answers.
grounding.eng: Injecting retrieved authoritative data into context so generations are traceable to sources.

multiagent.pm: A team of specialist agents over one do-everything agent — better for complex, multi-part work.
multiagent.eng: Decomposed task handled by specialized agents via coordinator/sequential/critic patterns.

agentops.pm: The operational discipline that keeps an agent reliable after launch — where most of the real work lives.
agentops.eng: Continuous eval, tracing, and metrics gating deploys; failures become regression cases.

guardrails.pm: The safety limits that let you trust an agent with real actions — your compliance and risk control.
guardrails.eng: Deterministic policy checks plus guard models wrapping tool calls and I/O; least privilege.

observability.pm: Being able to see inside an agent's decisions — the difference between debugging and guessing.
observability.eng: Logs, traces (per-run trajectory), and metrics; OpenTelemetry-style spans over the agent loop.

agentmemory.pm: What makes an agent feel personal and continuous instead of forgetting you every session.
agentmemory.eng: Short-term session state plus long-term store (usually vector-backed) with write/retrieve tools.

react.pm: The think-act-observe rhythm behind agents that tackle a task step by step.
react.eng: Interleaved reasoning + tool actions with observations fed back before the next step.

computeruse.pm: Automation for systems with no API — flexible, but slower and riskier than a real integration.
computeruse.eng: Vision-driven UI control (screenshot → click/type) over an app's interface; brittle, needs oversight.

agentidentity.pm: Treating each agent as its own accountable actor — the key to safe delegation at scale.
agentidentity.eng: Per-agent cryptographic identity (e.g., SPIFFE) with least-privilege IAM and audit trails.

vectordb.pm: The tech that powers "find similar" over your content — foundation for search, RAG, and memory.
vectordb.eng: Indexes embeddings for approximate nearest-neighbor lookup (cosine/dot) at scale.

agentpayments.pm: The nascent rails for agents to spend money safely — mostly a "watch this space" for now.
agentpayments.eng: AP2 signed intent mandates + x402 (HTTP 402) micropayments; early, non-standardized.

reasoningmodels.pm: Models that trade speed and cost for accuracy on hard, multi-step problems.
reasoningmodels.eng: Models trained to emit extended internal reasoning tokens before the answer; higher latency/cost.

trajectory.pm: Judging how an agent got there, not just whether the answer was right — key to real quality.
trajectory.eng: The ordered sequence of reasoning/tool/observation steps; unit of trajectory (glass-box) evaluation.

genai.pm: The category your product bets on — new content on demand; the question is where it adds value vs. novelty.
genai.eng: Models that sample new outputs from a learned distribution (LLMs, diffusion) rather than classify existing inputs.

machinelearning.pm: Software that improves from data instead of hand-written rules — plan for data collection and retraining.
machinelearning.eng: Algorithms that fit parameters to data to minimize a loss and generalize to unseen inputs.

deeplearning.pm: The approach behind modern AI capabilities — powerful, but data- and compute-hungry to build.
deeplearning.eng: Multi-layer neural networks trained via backprop; scales with data and GPU compute.

neuralnetwork.pm: The building block under most AI features — the learned model you ship and monitor.
neuralnetwork.eng: Layered weighted units with nonlinearities; parameters fit by gradient descent.

prompt.pm: The user-facing input that steers output quality — often your cheapest lever before any model change.
prompt.eng: The full input string (instructions, examples, context) conditioning next-token generation.

llm.pm: The core engine for text features — capable but probabilistic; design for review and failure modes.
llm.eng: Transformer trained on next-token prediction over large corpora; autoregressive decoding.

transformer.pm: The architecture that unlocked today's AI — mostly a build detail, but the reason capabilities jumped.
transformer.eng: Attention-based architecture enabling parallel sequence modeling; basis of modern LLMs.

gpt.pm: A leading model family to benchmark against — track versions for capability and cost shifts.
gpt.eng: OpenAI decoder-only transformer line; scaling parameters/data across generations.

chatgpt.pm: The product that set user expectations for AI chat — your baseline for UX and quality comparisons.
chatgpt.eng: Chat app over a GPT model, instruction-tuned with RLHF for dialogue.

gan.pm: Legacy image-gen tech — mostly relevant for context; new work uses diffusion.
gan.eng: Generator vs. discriminator adversarial training; largely superseded by diffusion for image synthesis.

diffusion.pm: The engine behind AI image features — plan for latency, safety filtering, and content rights.
diffusion.eng: Iterative denoising from noise conditioned on a prompt; stable to train, sampling-step heavy.

dalle.pm: A reference text-to-image product — useful for competitive and UX benchmarking.

texttoimage.pm: A feature pattern — describe, generate, iterate; watch prompt UX and rights/safety.
texttoimage.eng: Prompt-conditioned image generation trained on caption–image pairs, typically diffusion-based.

parameters.pm: A rough proxy for model size, cost, and capability — bigger isn't automatically better.
parameters.eng: Learned weights; count indicates capacity but data/method drive quality.

trainingdata.pm: The single biggest driver of behavior and bias — "what's it trained on?" is a product-risk question.
trainingdata.eng: Corpus fit during training; distribution and quality bound model behavior and failure modes.

inference.pm: The recurring per-use cost of AI features — the number that scales with adoption.
inference.eng: Forward-pass generation at serving time; dominant ongoing cost, latency-sensitive.

supervised.pm: Reliable when you can label data — budget for the labeling effort.
supervised.eng: Learning input→label mappings by minimizing loss against ground-truth labels.

unsupervised.pm: Finds structure without labels — good for discovery, fuzzier to evaluate.
unsupervised.eng: Learning structure from unlabeled data (clustering, self-supervised objectives).

reinforcementlearning.pm: Best when success is scorable but not labelable — powerful for optimization and agents.
reinforcementlearning.eng: Policy learning from reward signals via trial and error to maximize return.

rlhf.pm: The step that makes models feel helpful and on-brand — where alignment and tone get set.
rlhf.eng: Reward model from human preference rankings guides policy optimization of the base model.

overfitting.pm: The reason a model looks great in the demo and fails in production — insist on held-out evals.
overfitting.eng: Low training error, high generalization error; fit to noise rather than signal.

backprop.pm: A training internal — matters as the mechanism that makes learning (and its cost) possible.
backprop.eng: Gradient computation via the chain rule to update weights; core of neural-network training.

pretraining.pm: The expensive, general phase you usually buy rather than build — you adapt on top of it.
pretraining.eng: Large-scale self-supervised training that builds general capability before task adaptation.

foundationmodel.pm: Buy-vs-build pivot: adapt one general model across features instead of training per task.
foundationmodel.eng: Broadly pretrained model adapted (prompting/fine-tuning) to many downstream tasks.

multimodal.pm: Unlocks features that mix text, images, and audio — expands use cases and evaluation surface.
multimodal.eng: Shared representations across modalities enabling cross-modal input/output.

systemprompt.pm: The hidden instructions that set persona, rules, and safety — your main lever for controlling AI behavior.
systemprompt.eng: Prepended context with highest attention weight; defines persona, constraints, and output format.

attention.pm: The core mechanism that lets models understand context — mostly a build detail, but explains why long inputs cost more.
attention.eng: Scaled dot-product attention computing token-to-token relevance; O(n²) in sequence length.

moe.pm: Architecture that makes giant models affordable to run — big capacity without proportional cost increase.
moe.eng: Sparse gating routes tokens to k-of-n expert FFNs; high total params, low per-token compute.

lora.pm: The cheap way to customize a model to your needs — 90% less cost than full fine-tuning, easy to swap.
lora.eng: Low-rank trainable adapters injected into frozen attention layers; mergeable, stackable.

quantization.pm: What makes running models locally feasible — small quality trade for big cost and speed gains.
quantization.eng: Weight precision reduction (FP16→INT8/INT4); post-training or training-aware; GGUF for local serving.

distillation.pm: How you get frontier quality into a production-affordable model — train small from big.
distillation.eng: Student model trained on teacher logits/outputs; soft targets transfer richer signal than hard labels.

fewshot.pm: The fastest way to teach a model a new task — paste examples in the prompt, no training needed.
fewshot.eng: In-context exemplars that prime the model for a task; eats context window proportionally.

zeroshot.pm: When the model handles a task with no examples — the baseline you test before adding complexity.
zeroshot.eng: Task completion from instruction alone, no exemplars; relies on pretrained generalization.

incontext.pm: The reason prompt design matters so much — the model adapts on the fly from whatever you feed it.
incontext.eng: Emergent task adaptation from prompt content without gradient updates; mechanism debated.

chunking.pm: The invisible step that determines whether your search/RAG actually finds the right information.
chunking.eng: Document segmentation strategy before embedding; chunk size/overlap/boundary detection are key knobs.

semanticsearch.pm: Search that understands intent, not just keywords — the UX leap users expect now.
semanticsearch.eng: Query and documents embedded in shared vector space; ranked by cosine similarity.

alignment.pm: The work that makes AI trustworthy enough to ship — helpful, honest, and safe by design.
alignment.eng: Training techniques (RLHF, DPO, CAI) that steer model behavior toward human-intended outcomes.

dpo.pm: A simpler, cheaper way to align models — gaining ground over RLHF for many use cases.
dpo.eng: Preference-based alignment via classification loss; no reward model needed; often stabler than PPO.

redteaming.pm: The security audit for AI — find the failures before users do.
redteaming.eng: Adversarial probing for jailbreaks, harmful outputs, bias, and prompt-injection vectors.

syntheticdata.pm: AI-generated training data — faster and cheaper, but monitor for drift and collapse.
syntheticdata.eng: Model-generated examples for training/eval; risk of distribution collapse without real-data anchoring.

benchmark.pm: The standardized tests for comparing models — useful for shortlisting, dangerous as the only metric.
benchmark.eng: Fixed eval suites (MMLU, HumanEval, Arena) for cross-model comparison; watch for overfitting to public sets.

openweights.pm: Models you can host yourself — full control, privacy, no per-call fees, but you own the ops.
openweights.eng: Publicly released model weights (Llama, Mistral); self-hosted; often community-quantized.

langchain.pm: The most common framework for LLM apps — speeds up development but adds abstraction overhead.
langchain.eng: Python/JS framework composing LLM calls, retrievers, tools, and memory into chains/pipelines.

langgraph.pm: The leading framework for structured agent workflows — makes complex agent logic visible and debuggable.
langgraph.eng: Directed-graph state machine for agent orchestration; typed state, conditional edges, interrupt support.

huggingface.pm: The central hub for open AI — where models, datasets, and demos live. Essential to know.
huggingface.eng: Platform + Transformers library; model hub, datasets, tokenizers, and inference API.

ollama.pm: Run AI models locally with one command — privacy, no API costs, good for prototyping.
ollama.eng: CLI model runner; OpenAI-compatible local API; manages GGUF downloads and GPU memory.

scalinglaws.pm: The finding that more compute predictably buys more capability — the bet driving AI investment.
scalinglaws.eng: Power-law relationships between compute/data/params and loss; Chinchilla-optimal ratios.

aisafety.pm: The discipline of preventing AI harm — from bias audits to existential risk research.
aisafety.eng: Near-term: bias, toxicity, misuse mitigation. Long-term: alignment robustness, control, corrigibility.

stablediffusion.pm: The open-source image generator — free, customizable, runs locally, huge community.
stablediffusion.eng: Latent diffusion model; open weights; ControlNet/LoRA ecosystem; SDXL and community fine-tunes.

midjourney.pm: Premium AI art tool — best-in-class aesthetics, closed service, Discord/web interface.
midjourney.eng: Closed image-generation model; Discord bot API; emphasis on aesthetic quality over photorealism.

claude.pm: Anthropic's model family — strong reasoning, long context, safety-focused. Key competitor to evaluate.
claude.eng: Anthropic LLM family (Haiku/Sonnet/Opus); Constitutional AI alignment; native tool use and long context.

gemini.pm: Google's AI — natively multimodal, deeply integrated with Google Workspace and Search.
gemini.eng: Google multimodal model family (Flash/Pro/Ultra); native cross-modal training; tight GCP integration.

latentspace.pm: The internal representation where the model "thinks" — conceptually useful for understanding embeddings and generation.
latentspace.eng: Learned lower-dimensional manifold where input distributions are compressed and structured.

bias.pm: Systematic unfairness in AI output — a legal, ethical, and reputational risk that needs active monitoring.
bias.eng: Systematic skew from data/labeling/optimization; mitigate via diverse data, audits, disaggregated eval.

nlp.pm: The field behind every text AI feature — useful context for understanding what LLMs replaced and improved.
nlp.eng: Computational linguistics; pre-LLM: feature engineering + task-specific models; post-LLM: prompt-based.

bert.pm: The pre-LLM text understanding model — fading for new projects but still running in production for fast classification.
bert.eng: Bidirectional encoder transformer; masked language modeling; fast classification via fine-tuned heads.

copilot.pm: The AI-assistant pattern embedded in tools — drives adoption, sets UX expectations, lighter than full agents.
copilot.eng: In-tool LLM integration; context from editor/app state; suggestion-based UX with human acceptance.

transferlearning.pm: The reason fine-tuning works — broad knowledge transfers to specific tasks cheaply.
transferlearning.eng: Reusing pretrained representations; adapt final layers or add adapters for downstream tasks.

agenticframework.pm: The libraries that handle agent plumbing — pick one to move fast, evaluate carefully to avoid lock-in.
agenticframework.eng: Orchestration libraries (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen) abstracting the agent loop, tools, and memory.

constitutionalai.pm: Anthropic's approach to alignment — transparent, principle-based, less dependent on human labeling.
constitutionalai.eng: Self-critique against written principles + RLAIF; produces auditable alignment with less human annotation.

tokenizer.pm: The invisible text splitter that explains why AI miscounts letters and some languages cost more.
tokenizer.eng: BPE/SentencePiece converting text to token IDs; vocabulary size and merge rules affect cost and capability.

topptopk.pm: Output-shaping controls alongside temperature — useful knobs for tuning response quality.
topptopk.eng: Sampling truncation: top-k keeps k most likely tokens; top-p (nucleus) keeps cumulative-probability set.
